title: Marrow and split pea dal with broccoli

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain cupboard or garden staple: split peas, stock, curry powder, fresh vegetables and a lemon.

supermarket.reason: Split peas, marrow in August, broccoli and the rest are everyday items at an ordinary supermarket price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded saucepan and simple chopping and simmering.

works.reason: 250g split peas to 1.2l stock with a watery marrow should give a dal of the right consistency for four, and about 50 minutes of simmering will soften the peas.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers the chopping and frying the onion, and the marrow is peeled during the simmer, so the 55 minutes of cooking broadly matches the timed steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, and the steps use nothing that is not listed.

seasonal_feel.reason: A whole small marrow simmered into the dal makes the August glut the point of a gentle, lightly spiced lunch.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, homely British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Pulses with marrow and broccoli make a filling, wholesome lunch a family would happily eat again.
